title: merge joins on shop: sorted inputs from indexes or from Sorts, and rewinds over duplicate keys

steps.sql: SELECT id, name FROM customers WHERE id <= 5 ORDER BY id
steps.note: five customers, for the small join.

steps.sql: SELECT id, customer_id FROM orders WHERE id IN (1, 12, 47, 92, 511, 529, 566, 1596) ORDER BY id
steps.note: eight orders, some customers twice, one customer not in the list.

steps.sql:
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF)
SELECT o.id, o.status, oi.line_no, oi.qty
FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
ORDER BY o.id
steps.note: orders and their items, in order id order. both primary keys hand rows over sorted on order_id: a merge join with no sorting at all.

data: ->  Index Scan using orders_pkey on orders o (actual rows=10000.00 loops=1)
->  Index Scan using order_items_pkey on order_items oi (actual rows=24942.00 loops=1)

steps.sql:
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF)
SELECT c.id, c.name, o.id
FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
ORDER BY c.id
steps.note: customers and their orders, by customer. nothing hands orders over sorted by customer_id, so postgres hashes, then sorts all 10,000 rows for the ORDER BY.

data: ->  Seq Scan on orders o (actual rows=10000.00 loops=1)
->  Seq Scan on customers c (actual rows=2000.00 loops=1)

steps.note: orders joined to itself on customer_id, merge forced. the inner Sort hands over more rows than it holds: every run of duplicate keys is read again.

data: ->  Seq Scan on orders a (actual rows=10000.00 loops=1)
->  Seq Scan on orders b (actual rows=10000.00 loops=1)

steps.sql:
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF)
SELECT p.name, oi.qty FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON p.id = oi.product_id
steps.note: order lines and products, merge forced: both sides sorted first. the products side stops at 199 of 200 rows, because no order line wants product 200.

data: ->  Seq Scan on order_items oi (actual rows=24942.00 loops=1)
->  Seq Scan on products p (actual rows=200.00 loops=1)

steps.note: with an index on orders.customer_id, the by-customer join needs no Sort and no hash: two index scans, merged.

data: ->  Index Scan using customers_pkey on customers c (actual rows=2000.00 loops=1)
->  Index Scan using orders_customer_id_idx on orders o (actual rows=10000.00 loops=1)

steps.note: the self-join again, now over the index. an index scan can step back, but each step back fetches the rows again, so a Materialize keeps the current run in memory instead.

data: ->  Index Scan using orders_customer_id_idx on orders a (actual rows=10000.00 loops=1)
->  Index Scan using orders_customer_id_idx on orders b (actual rows=10000.00 loops=1)
